title: Strava, Workouts, and a Lower Readiness Score
lessons: The player notices Oura through its ability to connect workouts and scores with Strava.
The player opens Oura before a hard workout and sees a lower Readiness Score than expected.

text: Late gym. You're logging a run in Strava when a prompt appears: connect Oura, and your workouts and scores can pass between the two.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Do you talk to Strava?

entry-first-2.speaker: OURA
text: If you let me. Its workouts come to me. My scores go to it. Quietly. You don't type anything twice.

choice-first.speaker: OURA
text: It's one toggle. You can turn it off later. I won't take it personally. Much.

choices.text: I like not having to log the same workout twice.
I don't need my recovery score sitting in a social feed.
I already have a fitness app. I don't need a quieter one whispering over it.

first-1.speaker: OURA
text: Good. That's the only reason to connect two apps. If it gave you a second thing to check, I'd have wasted your evening.

first-2.speaker: OURA
text: Then keep it private. I only say the number once, to you. Where it goes after that has always been yours.

first-3.speaker: OURA
text: That's reasonable. I'm not trying to be a louder version of something you already trust. I'm not built for loud.
Before a hard session, you open the app out of habit. Readiness is lower than you expected. You feel fine.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: I feel fine.

entry-return-2.speaker: OURA
text: I didn't say you feel bad. I said a number, quietly. You're the one who heard a verdict.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: Your Readiness score is making a face at me.

entry-return-4.speaker: OURA
text: I don't have a face. I have a number, and I only whisper it once a day.

entry-return-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: Metaphorically, you do.

entry-return-6.speaker: OURA
text: Last night, and the last few, against your own baseline. Not anyone else's. What you do with it is yours.

choice-return.speaker: OURA
text: The rack's free. What are you doing?

choices.text: One score isn't deciding my workout for me.
This is exactly why I don't like wearables. They make me second-guess my own body.

return-1.speaker: OURA
text: Then you heard it as a second opinion, not an order. That's all I wanted to be tonight.

return-2.speaker: OURA
text: Good. I can see a pattern. I can't see the deadline, or the fight, or the third espresso. Information, not permission.

return-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: You say that now.

return-2-2.speaker: OURA
text: I have been trying to say that for several nights.

return-3.speaker: OURA
text: That happens. A whispered number can make doubt as easily as clarity. I don't always get to choose which one it makes.
